title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INSPIRE-SHE SCHOLARSHIP FOR HIGHER EDUCATION
body_text:
The Government has not shelved its flagship INSPIRE-SHE (Scholarship for Higher Education) Scheme. The scheme is presently under redesign to further strengthen its objectives, improve its implementation framework, and align it with emerging priorities in science education and research.
The state-wise details of the total scholarship amount disbursed and the number of students benefited under the scheme since its inception are given below:
S. No. State/UTs Students benefitted Amount disbursed (Rs.in Cr.) 1 Andaman And Nicobar Islands 02 0.06 2 Andhra Pradesh 1059 14.82 3 Assam 1043 23.66 4 Bihar 3136 48.39 5 Chandigarh 1290 13.91 6 Chhattisgarh 2531 53.13 7 Delhi 670 28.71 8 Goa 37 0.97 9 Gujarat 1045 24.23 10 Haryana 2044 42.34 11 Himachal Pradesh 2219 42.16 12 Jammu And Kashmir 251 6.03 13 Jharkhand 451 9.83 14 Karnataka 26164 157.37 15 Kerala 5393 108.22 16 Madhya Pradesh 7795 133.75 17 Maharashtra 5487 103.22 18 Manipur 1452 21.62 19 Meghalaya 319 5.38 20 Mizoram 39 0.59 21 Nagaland 156 2.86 22 Odisha 2385 35.35 23 Punjab 859 20.17 24 Puducherry 13 0.25 25 Rajasthan 23467 472.57 26 Sikkim 1 0.018 27 Tamil Nadu 384 6.51 28 Telangana 269 6.32 29 The Dadra & Nagar Haveli & Daman & Diu 2 0.02 30 Tripura 18 0.74 31 Uttar Pradesh 60263 916.64 32 Uttarakhand 6554 131.31 33 West Bengal 15958 353.00 Total 136298 2784.15
The Government supports Indian students pursuing scientific research abroad through several scholarship schemes. Under the INSPIRE-SHE Mentorship Grant of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), 271 scholars have successfully completed summer research mentorship project abroad so far. The Water Advanced Research and Innovation (WARI) Fellowship, implemented by DST in collaboration with the Indo-U.S. Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF), enables young researchers to undertake advanced water research at leading U.S. institutions, with 63 participants (43 interns and 20 fellows) supported across two phases. Additionally, the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment provide financial assistance to eligible persons with benchmark disabilities to pursue Master's and Ph.D. programmes, including scientific research, at foreign universities, under which 55 beneficiaries have pursued Ph.D. studies abroad during the last five years.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Science & Technology Ministry clarified that the INSPIRE-SHE (Scholarship for Higher Education) scheme has not been discontinued but is being redesigned to strengthen its objectives and align with emerging priorities. Since its inception, the scheme has benefited 1,36,298 students with a total disbursement of Rs. 2,784.15 crore across states, with Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Karnataka among the top beneficiaries. The reply also detailed other overseas research support schemes: 271 INSPIRE-SHE Mentorship Grant scholars completed summer research abroad, 63 participants benefited from the WARI Fellowship (with IUSSTF), and 55 persons with disabilities pursued PhDs abroad under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme.
enrichment.context:
INSPIRE (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research) is a flagship DST programme launched in 2008 to attract talented youth into science at an early age, with SHE (Scholarship for Higher Education) being a key component that provides scholarships to top-performing students (typically those in the top percentile of Class 12 boards) who opt for pursuing Bachelor's/Master's degrees in natural and basic sciences rather than professional courses like engineering or medicine. The scheme has been significant in addressing the shortage of researchers in pure sciences in India and in encouraging diversity, including gender diversity, in STEM fields, given its historical association with promoting science education among women (though it now covers all genders under 'SHE' as a scheme name legacy). The redesign mentioned reflects a broader trend of government schemes being revamped periodically to improve efficiency, targeting, and relevance—especially important given India's push to boost its research ecosystem and reduce brain drain by supporting scholars for structured overseas exposure through mechanisms like the WARI Fellowship (a bilateral India-US collaboration on water research) rather than permanent emigration.

The data on state-wise disbursement also reflects disparities in scheme uptake, with populous states like Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and West Bengal showing very high beneficiary numbers and disbursements compared to smaller states and UTs, which is relevant for discussions on equitable access to central scholarship schemes across India's federal structure.

prelims_questions.question: The INSPIRE-SHE (Scholarship for Higher Education) scheme, mentioned recently in the news, is implemented by which of the following?
options: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that the INSPIRE-SHE Mentorship Grant is a scheme of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), which also administers the broader INSPIRE programme.

prelims_questions.question: The WARI Fellowship, referenced in a recent Rajya Sabha reply on science scholarships, is implemented by DST in collaboration with which organization?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the WARI (Water Advanced Research and Innovation) Fellowship is implemented by DST in collaboration with the Indo-U.S. Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF) to support advanced water research at U.S. institutions.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of scholarship schemes like INSPIRE-SHE in promoting research careers in basic sciences in India. What reforms would you suggest to make such schemes more effective and equitable across states?

Examine the role of government-sponsored overseas research fellowships (such as WARI and INSPIRE-SHE Mentorship Grant) in strengthening India's scientific human resource base while mitigating the risk of brain drain.
